fun_facts: Pompano grow fast enough, and are prized enough, that they're now farmed commercially in offshore cages: going from hatchling to a pound or more in under a year makes them one of the few marine finfish it's currently profitable to raise instead of just catch.

A moving school of pompano gives itself away before a hook ever gets wet. The fish periodically skip and flip clear of the surf, a habit surf anglers use to spot 'nervous water' and find the school from the beach.
Pompano hunt buried sand fleas and mole crabs mostly by feel: a dense patch of pores along the lower jaw and lateral line reads the vibration of prey digging into the sand as a wave washes back out.

not_taggable.reason: a fish in poor condition or bleeding is unlikely to survive release, so tagging it wastes the tag and the reward

must_release.reason: under the 11-inch minimum used for Florida pompano across the South Atlantic and Gulf coasts; South Carolina currently sets no size limit of its own for this species
